newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: ABB confident of Bakun project.
newsitem.headline: ABB confident of Bakun project.

text.p: ABB Asea Brown Boveri Ltd said on Tuesday it was confident about the viability of Malaysia's Bakun hydro-electric dam and of getting timely payments for carrying out its part of the project.
"This is a solid project built on its own merit after a 20-year study," ABB's president and chief executive officer Goran Lindahl told reporters at a briefing on the company's activities.
ABB and Brazil's Companhia Brasileria Projectos e Obras (CBPO) have the contract to design and build the controversial 13.6 billion ringgit dam in the eastern state of Sarawak.
In response to a question, Lindahl said ABB has bank guarantees on receiving payment from the dam's backers even if the project was to run into financial difficulties.
He said payments for the works are backed by shareholders of the dam's operating company, Bakun Hydro-Electric Corp (BHEC).

The main shareholders of BHEC are infrastructure developer Ekran Bhd with a 32 percent stake, power firm Tenaga Nasional Bhd (five percent), Malaysia's national pension fund (five percent) and state investment arm Khazanah Holdings Bhd (five percent).

Some environmentalists have opposed the massive project. The dam came under renewed scrutiny after talk emerged this week that Ekran may scrap a plan to offer shares in the project to foreign investors due to lukewarm response.
The project's initial public offering adviser, Commerce International Merchant Bankers Bhd, told Reuters on Monday that the IPO has attracted interest from local and foreign investors.
Lindahl said ABB's portion of the works is likely to start "in the next few months" after recent completion of tunnelling works to divert a river.
The Swiss-Swedish group has about 200 staff preparing the groundwork for the 2,400 megawatt capacity dam, Lindahl said.

ABB's portion of the works include supplying six 420 megawatt hydro-generators, a 500-kilovolt high voltage direct-current transmission system, installing the record-setting 650-km (400-mile) long submarine cable to connect the dam to Peninsular Malaysia and civil works with CBPO.
Lindahl said he expects only a four percent power transmission loss despite the distance between the generation point in Sarawak and its destination on Peninsular Malaysia.
The project is scheduled to be completed by 2003.
